title: SPF decoded
caption: SPF numbers measure how long a sunscreen extends your skin's resistance to UVB rays — the burning rays — not how much protection you get overall. A higher number filters marginally more UV, but the bigger gap in the UAE is that most people apply a quarter of the tested dose, which drops effective SPF by roughly two-thirds regardless of what's on the label. Dubai compounds this differently than cooler climates: UV Index regularly hits 11+ between May and September, you're moving in and out of aggressive air conditioning that dries the skin barrier, and glass in cars and offices blocks UVB but lets UVA through. UVA is the ray that drives pigmentation and collagen breakdown without producing a visible burn — so you can feel fine and still accumulate skin damage over a summer. Broad-spectrum coverage means a product is tested against both UVB and UVA, and PA+++ or four-star UVA ratings are the markings that confirm UVA protection is meaningful. Knowing those two labels means you can read any sunscreen shelf without guesswork. Not medical advice, just the honest basics. Learn more at cliniclick.ae/concerns/pigmentation/what-is-pigmentation
